varieties.name: Yukon Gold
varieties.description: Yukon Gold Potato is a well-loved potato variety known for its buttery flavor and smooth, creamy texture. With a bushy growth habit, it produces attractive tubers with golden-yellow skin and rich yellow flesh. This mid-season variety is commonly grown as an annual for its delectable and versatile culinary uses, excelling in nearly every cooking method.

care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Balanced fertilizer at planting, side-dress when plants are 6 inches tall

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Rich, buttery, slightly sweet with a creamy, moist texture

root_characteristics.storage_life: 2-3 months in cool, dark, humid conditions

varieties.fun_fact: Yukon Gold Potatoes were developed in the 1960s at the University of Guelph in Ontario, Canada. They quickly gained popularity for their rich flavor, golden color, and ability to hold their shape well during cooking, making them one of the most versatile potatoes available.
varieties.planting_tip: For successful cultivation of Yukon Gold Potatoes, start with certified seed potatoes cut into 2-ounce pieces with at least 2 eyes each. Plant in loose, well-draining soil with good fertility. Hill the soil around the base of the plants as they grow to encourage more tuber development and prevent greening. Provide consistent moisture, especially during tuber formation. Harvest new potatoes 2-3 weeks after flowering, or wait until foliage yellows for full-sized potatoes. Cure harvested potatoes in a dark, ventilated area for 1-2 weeks before storing.

varieties.name: Russet Burbank
varieties.description: Russet Burbank Potato is a classic late-season potato variety known for its large size, oblong shape, and distinctive russeted brown skin. It has a fluffy, dry texture when cooked, making it ideal for baking, frying, and mashing. Russet Burbank is the most widely grown potato variety in North America and is used extensively in commercial production for french fries, baked potatoes, and mashed potatoes.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, 1-2 inches per week, reduce near harvest
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Balanced fertilizer at planting, avoid excess nitrogen

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, earthy flavor with a fluffy, dry, starchy texture

root_characteristics.storage_life: 4-6 months in proper cool, dark storage

varieties.fun_fact: Russet Burbank Potato is the most widely grown potato variety in the United States and is the potato of choice for McDonald's french fries. It was developed by Luther Burbank in the 1870s and has dominated the commercial potato market for over a century.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Russet Burbank seed pieces in well-drained, loose soil with a pH of 5.0-6.0. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant seed pieces 4 inches deep and 12-15 inches apart in rows spaced 30-36 inches apart. Hill soil around plants every 2-3 weeks to prevent greening. Maintain consistent moisture but avoid overwatering, especially near harvest, to prevent hollow heart and other defects. This variety requires a long growing season for best tuber size.

varieties.name: Red Pontiac
varieties.description: Red Pontiac Potato is a popular early to mid-season red-skinned potato variety known for its vibrant red color, smooth thin skin, and creamy white flesh. It has shallow eyes and produces round to oblong tubers. Red Pontiac is versatile and can be used in a variety of dishes, including mashed potatoes, potato salads, and roasted potatoes. It is prized for its attractive appearance, waxy texture, and rich flavor.

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, slightly sweet with a creamy, waxy texture

root_characteristics.texture: Creamy, waxy, holds shape when cooked

varieties.fun_fact: Red Pontiac Potato is a favorite among home gardeners and is known for its high yields, disease resistance, and ability to thrive in various soil conditions. It's one of the most reliable red potato varieties for beginning gardeners.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Red Pontiac seed pieces in well-drained, loose soil. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant seed pieces 4 inches deep and 10-12 inches apart in rows spaced 24-30 inches apart. This variety is more tolerant of heavy soils than russet types. Hill plants regularly to encourage tuber formation and prevent greening. Red Pontiac produces well even in less-than-ideal conditions, making it excellent for beginning gardeners.

varieties.name: Kennebec
varieties.description: Kennebec Potato is a popular mid-season potato variety known for its large size, smooth buff-colored skin, and bright white flesh. It has very shallow eyes and a uniform oval shape, making it ideal for processing into french fries and potato chips. Kennebec also works exceptionally well for mashed potatoes, baking, and boiling. It is favored by commercial growers for its high yields, excellent storage qualities, and broad disease resistance.

care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Balanced fertilizer at planting and mid-season

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, clean flavor with all-purpose texture, slightly waxy to mealy

root_characteristics.root_color: Light buff to tan skin, white flesh

varieties.fun_fact: Kennebec Potato was developed at the USDA research station in Maine in 1948 and quickly became one of the most popular varieties for both home gardeners and commercial growers. Its excellent disease resistance and storage capabilities made it a staple in American agriculture.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Kennebec seed pieces in well-drained, loose soil. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant seed pieces 4 inches deep and 12-15 inches apart in rows spaced 30-36 inches apart. This variety benefits from consistent moisture throughout the growing season. Hill plants regularly to maximize yield and prevent tuber greening. Kennebec is known for its reliability and consistent production across varying growing conditions.

varieties.name: All Blue
varieties.description: All Blue Potato, also known as Purple Peruvian, is a unique heirloom potato variety with deep blue-purple skin and vibrant purple flesh that holds its color when cooked. It has a rich, nutty flavor and moist, creamy texture, making it ideal for mashed potatoes, salads, and roasted dishes. All Blue Potato is prized for its striking appearance and high levels of antioxidant anthocyanins.

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Rich, earthy, nutty flavor with a moist, waxy texture

varieties.fun_fact: All Blue Potato gets its vibrant purple color from natural anthocyanin pigments, which also provide antioxidant benefits. The color intensifies when cooked, making it a stunning addition to any dish. It's an ancient variety from South America.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant All Blue seed pieces in well-drained, loose soil. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant seed pieces 4 inches deep and 10-12 inches apart in rows spaced 24-30 inches apart. This variety may produce smaller yields than standard varieties but makes up for it with its unique color and flavor. The purple color is most vibrant when potatoes are steamed or roasted rather than boiled.

varieties.name: Adirondack Blue
varieties.description: Adirondack Blue Potato is a modern blue potato variety with deep blue-purple skin and vibrant blue flesh that retains its color better than other blue varieties when cooked. It has a rich, earthy flavor and moist, creamy texture, making it ideal for mashed potatoes, salads, and roasted dishes. Developed at Cornell University, Adirondack Blue is prized for its striking appearance, nutritional benefits from anthocyanin pigments, and improved disease resistance.

care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Balanced fertilizer at planting and mid-season

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Rich, earthy, slightly nutty with a moist, creamy texture

varieties.fun_fact: Adirondack Blue Potato is named after the Adirondack Mountains in New York state, where it was developed by researchers at Cornell University. It was specifically bred to have higher anthocyanin content than other blue varieties and to retain its vibrant color better during cooking.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Adirondack Blue seed pieces in well-drained, loose soil. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant seed pieces 4 inches deep and 10-12 inches apart in rows spaced 24-30 inches apart. This variety has better disease resistance than many heirloom blue potatoes. The flesh color is most vibrant when cooked using dry heat methods like roasting or baking.

varieties.name: German Butterball
varieties.description: German Butterball Potato is a beloved heirloom potato variety with golden-yellow skin and rich, buttery golden-yellow flesh. It has a creamy, dense texture and exceptionally rich, nutty flavor when cooked, making it ideal for mashed potatoes, baked potatoes, and roasting. German Butterball is prized for its smooth skin, round to oval shape, shallow eyes, and excellent storage qualities. This variety is considered by many to be one of the best-tasting potatoes available.

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Rich, buttery, nutty with exceptional flavor, creamy and moist texture

root_characteristics.storage_life: 4-5 months in proper cool, dark storage

varieties.fun_fact: German Butterball Potato is a favorite among home gardeners and chefs and is often described as having the richest, most buttery flavor of any potato variety. Despite its name, it was actually developed in the United States, not Germany, but the 'German' refers to its style and flavor profile.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant German Butterball seed pieces in well-drained, loose soil. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant seed pieces 4 inches deep and 10-12 inches apart in rows spaced 24-30 inches apart. This variety benefits from consistent moisture and produces the best flavor when allowed to fully mature. Let the soil dry slightly between waterings to concentrate sugars and enhance flavor. Cure properly for best storage and flavor development.

varieties.name: Fingerling French
varieties.description: Fingerling French Potato is a distinctive heirloom fingerling variety with rose-red skin and vibrant yellow flesh. These small, elongated tubers have a firm, waxy texture and a rich, nutty, buttery flavor that intensifies when roasted. The finger-like shape (2-4 inches long) makes them perfect for roasting whole, grilling, or showcasing in potato salads. Fingerling French is prized by gourmet cooks for its beautiful presentation, excellent flavor, and ability to hold its shape during cooking.

care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Balanced fertilizer at planting, light feeding mid-season

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Rich, nutty, buttery with intense flavor, firm and waxy texture

varieties.fun_fact: Fingerling potatoes get their name from their resemblance to fingers. French Fingerling, despite its name, is believed to have originated in Germany or Austria. They became popular in French cuisine and were brought to America by European immigrants. Fingerlings command premium prices at farmers markets due to their gourmet appeal and labor-intensive harvest.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Fingerling French seed pieces in well-drained, loose soil enriched with organic matter. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant whole small tubers or cut larger ones, spacing 8-10 inches apart in rows 24-30 inches apart. These smaller potatoes don't need as much space as standard varieties. Hill lightly to prevent greening but avoid excessive hilling which can reduce tuber formation. Harvest carefully to avoid breaking the delicate tubers. Best harvested when fully mature for optimal flavor and texture.

varieties.name: Purple Majesty
varieties.description: Purple Majesty Potato is a modern variety developed by Colorado State University, featuring deep purple skin and vibrant purple flesh throughout. This oblong potato maintains its striking purple color even after cooking, making it perfect for adding visual interest to any dish. Purple Majesty has a mild, slightly earthy flavor and medium-moist texture. It's packed with anthocyanin antioxidants and offers excellent disease resistance, making it both nutritious and easy to grow.

care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Balanced fertilizer at planting and mid-season

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, slightly earthy with subtle sweetness, medium-moist texture

varieties.fun_fact: Purple Majesty was specifically bred to have deep purple color throughout the entire tuber, unlike some purple varieties that have white areas. The intense purple color comes from very high levels of anthocyanins - up to 4 times more than other purple varieties. These antioxidants have been studied for potential health benefits including anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular support.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Purple Majesty seed pieces in well-drained soil with good organic content. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant seed pieces 4 inches deep and 10-12 inches apart in rows spaced 30 inches apart. This variety has excellent disease resistance, making it easier to grow organically. The purple color is most vibrant when cooked using methods that preserve pigments - steaming or microwaving works better than boiling. Hill plants regularly to maximize yield and prevent greening.

varieties.name: Norland Red
varieties.description: Norland Red Potato is a popular early-season red potato variety known for its bright red skin, white flesh, and round to oblong shape. This variety matures quickly and produces smooth-skinned tubers with shallow eyes, making them easy to clean and prepare. Norland has a waxy texture that holds its shape well during cooking, making it ideal for potato salads, boiling, and roasting. It's prized for early harvest, reliable production, and good disease resistance.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, 1-2 inches per week, especially during tuber formation
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Balanced fertilizer at planting, light feeding at emergence

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, slightly sweet with waxy, creamy texture

root_characteristics.texture: Waxy, holds shape well when cooked

varieties.fun_fact: Norland Red was developed in North Dakota in 1957 and quickly became one of the most popular early red potato varieties in North America. Its ability to produce a crop in just 65-70 days makes it perfect for northern climates with short growing seasons. Many gardeners plant Norland for early 'new potatoes' and then plant a second crop for fall harvest.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Norland Red seed pieces in early spring as soon as soil can be worked, as it's cold-tolerant and benefits from cool growing conditions. Plant in well-drained soil 3-4 inches deep and 10-12 inches apart in rows spaced 24-30 inches apart. This variety sets tubers early, so ensure adequate moisture during the first 6-8 weeks. Can be harvested as 'new potatoes' 50-60 days after planting, or allow to mature fully. Excellent choice for succession planting or double-cropping in areas with long seasons.

varieties.name: Carola
varieties.description: Carola Potato is a premium mid-season variety from Germany, featuring smooth golden-yellow skin and rich, deep yellow flesh. This variety is renowned for its exceptional buttery flavor, creamy texture, and versatility in cooking. Carola produces uniform, oval tubers with shallow eyes and has excellent culinary qualities for boiling, mashing, roasting, and making gourmet potato dishes. It's a favorite among chefs and serious gardeners for its superior taste and consistent performance.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, 1-2 inches per week, consistent moisture important
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Balanced fertilizer at planting, side-dress when plants reach 6 inches

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Exceptionally buttery, rich, and creamy with sweet undertones, waxy to all-purpose texture

root_characteristics.storage_life: 3-5 months in proper cool, dark storage

varieties.fun_fact: Carola is considered by many European chefs to be one of the finest-tasting potatoes available and commands premium prices in markets. It was developed in Germany in the 1980s and has won numerous taste awards. The deep yellow color indicates high carotenoid content, and the flavor is so rich that these potatoes need minimal seasoning. Carola is often compared favorably to Yukon Gold but with even better flavor.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Carola seed pieces in loose, well-drained soil enriched with compost. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant seed pieces 4 inches deep and 12-15 inches apart in rows spaced 30-36 inches apart. Carola benefits from consistent moisture throughout the growing season - uneven watering can cause growth cracks. Hill plants regularly to encourage maximum tuber development. Allow tubers to fully mature for best flavor and storage qualities. Cure properly after harvest for 10-14 days to enhance flavor and storage life.

varieties.name: Russian Banana
varieties.description: Russian Banana Potato is an heirloom fingerling variety with distinctive yellow, crescent-shaped tubers that resemble small bananas. This late-season variety produces firm, waxy potatoes with rich, buttery yellow flesh and exceptional flavor. Russian Banana has a dense, creamy texture that holds its shape perfectly during cooking, making it ideal for potato salads, roasting, and grilling. The unique shape and outstanding flavor have made it a favorite at farmers markets and among gourmet cooks.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, 1-2 inches per week, consistent moisture
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate fertilizer at planting, light mid-season feeding

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Rich, buttery, nutty with exceptional depth of flavor, firm and waxy

root_characteristics.texture: Dense, firm, waxy, holds shape excellently
root_characteristics.storage_life: 4-6 months in proper cool, dark storage

varieties.fun_fact: Russian Banana Potato is believed to have been brought to North America by Russian immigrants in the late 1800s, possibly via Alaska. Despite its heirloom status, it wasn't widely available until Seed Savers Exchange helped preserve and distribute it in the 1980s. The crescent shape develops naturally and is one of the most distinctive of all fingerling varieties. Russian Banana is known for having one of the longest storage lives of any fingerling potato.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Russian Banana seed pieces or whole small tubers in well-drained, loose soil. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant 3-4 inches deep and 8-10 inches apart in rows spaced 24-30 inches apart. This late-season variety needs a long growing season to develop full flavor and size. Provide consistent moisture throughout growth but reduce watering 2 weeks before harvest. The firm, waxy texture makes these potatoes excellent for storage - cure properly for 2 weeks and store in cool (40-45°F), dark conditions. Handle carefully during harvest as the elongated shape can be fragile.

varieties.name: Beauregard
varieties.description: Beauregard Sweet Potato is a popular and widely grown sweet potato variety known for its sweet flavor and vibrant orange flesh. With vining growth, it produces tubers that are excellent for baking, roasting, or mashing. While technically a perennial, it is commonly grown as an annual for its delicious and versatile culinary uses.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, especially during tuber formation

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, moist, and creamy

varieties.fun_fact: Beauregard Sweet Potato was developed by researchers at the Louisiana Agricultural Experiment Station and released in 1987. It quickly became one of the most popular sweet potato varieties due to its excellent taste and high yield.
varieties.planting_tip: For successful cultivation of Beauregard Sweet Potato, start with healthy slips. Plant in loose, well-draining soil with a slightly acidic to neutral pH. Provide consistent moisture, especially during the tuber-forming period. Harvest when the leaves start to yellow and the tubers have reached a desirable size. Cure harvested sweet potatoes in a warm, humid place (80-85°F) for 7-10 days before storing in a cool, dark area.

varieties.name: Jewel
varieties.description: Jewel Sweet Potato is a popular variety known for its vibrant orange flesh and excellent flavor. It has reddish-purple skin and a moist, sweet flavor when cooked. Jewel sweet potatoes are versatile and can be used in a variety of dishes, including soups, salads, and desserts. They are prized for their attractive appearance and rich flavor.

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, moist, and flavorful

varieties.fun_fact: Jewel Sweet Potato was developed by researchers at Louisiana State University and released in 1965. It is known for its high yields and disease resistance.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Jewel Sweet Potato slips in well-drained, loose soil. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant slips about 3 inches deep and 12 inches apart in rows spaced 36-42 inches apart. Keep the soil consistently moist but not waterlogged.

varieties.name: Covington
varieties.description: Covington Sweet Potato is a popular variety known for its uniform shape, deep orange flesh, and excellent flavor. It has rose-colored skin and a moist, sweet flavor when cooked. Covington sweet potatoes are versatile and can be used in a variety of dishes, including fries, casseroles, and pies. They are prized for their consistent yields and disease resistance.

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, moist, and rich

varieties.fun_fact: Covington Sweet Potato was developed by researchers at North Carolina State University and released in 2005. It is known for its high yields and excellent disease resistance.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Covington Sweet Potato slips in well-drained, loose soil. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant slips about 3 inches deep and 12 inches apart in rows spaced 36-42 inches apart. Keep the soil consistently moist but not waterlogged.

varieties.name: Carolina Ruby
varieties.description: Carolina Ruby Sweet Potato is a popular heirloom variety known for its deep red-purple skin and moist, sweet flesh. It has a rich flavor and creamy texture when cooked, making it ideal for baking, boiling, or roasting. Carolina Ruby sweet potatoes are versatile and can be used in a variety of dishes, including pies, casseroles, and soups.

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Rich, sweet, and creamy

varieties.fun_fact: Carolina Ruby Sweet Potato is an heirloom variety that has been grown for generations in the southern United States. It is prized for its flavor and versatility in cooking.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Carolina Ruby Sweet Potato slips in well-drained, loose soil. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant slips about 3 inches deep and 12 inches apart in rows spaced 36-42 inches apart. Keep the soil consistently moist but not waterlogged.

varieties.name: O'Henry
varieties.description: O'Henry Sweet Potato is a popular variety known for its creamy texture and sweet flavor. It has pale copper skin and light cream-colored flesh. O'Henry sweet potatoes are versatile and can be used in a variety of dishes, including fries, casseroles, and pies. They are prized for their smooth texture and excellent flavor.

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, creamy, and mild

root_characteristics.root_color: Light cream-colored flesh, pale copper skin

varieties.fun_fact: O'Henry Sweet Potato is named after Henry, a laborer who discovered this variety in 1981 while working in a North Carolina field.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant O'Henry Sweet Potato slips in well-drained, loose soil. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant slips about 3 inches deep and 12 inches apart in rows spaced 36-42 inches apart. Keep the soil consistently moist but not waterlogged.

varieties.name: Japanese
varieties.description: Japanese Sweet Potato, also known as Satsumaimo, is a popular variety known for its purple skin and creamy white flesh. It has a slightly sweet flavor and moist texture when cooked, making it ideal for baking, steaming, or frying. Japanese Sweet Potato is versatile and can be used in a variety of dishes, including tempura, pies, and soups.

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Slightly sweet, nutty, and chestnut-like

varieties.fun_fact: Japanese Sweet Potato is a popular ingredient in Japanese cuisine and is often enjoyed roasted as a street food snack called 'yaki-imo'.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Japanese Sweet Potato slips in well-drained, loose soil. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant slips about 3 inches deep and 12 inches apart in rows spaced 36-42 inches apart. Keep the soil consistently moist but not waterlogged.

varieties.name: Purple
varieties.description: Purple Sweet Potato, also known as Okinawan Sweet Potato, is a unique variety known for its vibrant purple flesh and sweet flavor. It has a creamy texture when cooked and can be used in a variety of dishes, including mashed potatoes, pies, and desserts. Purple Sweet Potato is prized for its antioxidant-rich pigments and health benefits.

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, nutty, and slightly floral

root_characteristics.root_color: Vibrant purple flesh, light tan to purple skin

varieties.fun_fact: Purple Sweet Potato is native to the island of Okinawa in Japan and is a staple food in the Okinawan diet, known for promoting longevity and health.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Purple Sweet Potato slips in well-drained, loose soil. Choose a sunny location for optimal growth. Plant slips about 3 inches deep and 12 inches apart in rows spaced 36-42 inches apart. Keep the soil consistently moist but not waterlogged.

varieties.name: Georgia Jet
varieties.description: Georgia Jet Sweet Potato is a fast-maturing variety known for its deep orange flesh and copper-red skin. This early-season sweet potato was specifically bred for northern climates with shorter growing seasons, producing good yields in just 90-100 days. Georgia Jet has a moist, sweet flavor and smooth texture when cooked, making it excellent for baking, roasting, and mashing. It's prized for its adaptability to cooler climates and reliable production.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, especially during tuber formation

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, moist, and flavorful with rich orange color

varieties.fun_fact: Georgia Jet was developed specifically for northern gardeners who want to grow sweet potatoes but have shorter growing seasons. It can produce a crop in areas where other sweet potato varieties won't mature. The variety was released in 1982 and quickly became popular among home gardeners in USDA zones 5-7.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Georgia Jet slips in late spring when soil temperature reaches at least 60°F. This variety is more tolerant of cooler soil than most sweet potatoes. Plant slips 3-4 inches deep and 12 inches apart in well-drained, loose soil. Use black plastic mulch in northern climates to warm soil and extend the growing season. Georgia Jet's shorter maturity time makes it ideal for areas with 100-110 frost-free days. Harvest before first frost and cure at 80-85°F for 7-10 days.

varieties.name: Vardaman
varieties.description: Vardaman Sweet Potato is a unique bush-type variety with compact growth habit, making it ideal for small gardens and container growing. Unlike most sweet potatoes that produce long vines, Vardaman's vines stay short and manageable at 2-3 feet. It produces golden-orange flesh with rose-copper skin and has excellent flavor. The compact growth and attractive purple-tinged foliage make it popular for ornamental edible gardens while still providing good yields of delicious sweet potatoes.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, keep soil consistently moist

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, moist, and rich with excellent flavor

varieties.fun_fact: Vardaman is a breakthrough variety released in 1981 by Mississippi State University. It was the first successful bush-type sweet potato, revolutionizing sweet potato growing for small gardens. The compact habit uses only 20-30% of the space required by vining varieties, making it possible to grow sweet potatoes in raised beds, small gardens, and even large containers. The purple-tinged foliage is ornamental enough for landscape use.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Vardaman slips in well-drained soil or large containers filled with quality potting mix. Space slips 12-18 inches apart - much closer than vining varieties. The compact growth makes this variety ideal for intensive planting in raised beds. Plant slips 3 inches deep when soil temperature reaches 65°F. Container growing requires consistent watering and feeding. Despite smaller plant size, Vardaman produces surprisingly good yields. Perfect for small-space gardening, patios, and anywhere traditional sweet potato vines would be too aggressive.

varieties.name: Murasaki
varieties.description: Murasaki Sweet Potato is a Japanese variety featuring stunning purple skin and white flesh with purple streaks. This unique sweet potato has a dry, fluffy texture similar to a russet potato and a mild, slightly sweet, chestnut-like flavor. Murasaki is less sweet than typical orange sweet potatoes, making it versatile for both sweet and savory dishes. It's particularly popular in Japanese and Hawaiian cuisines and is prized for its beautiful appearance and distinctive texture.

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, slightly sweet, nutty, chestnut-like with dry, fluffy texture

root_characteristics.root_color: White flesh with purple streaks, deep purple skin

varieties.fun_fact: Murasaki means 'purple' in Japanese. This variety is extremely popular in Hawaii where it's often called 'Hawaiian Sweet Potato' and is used in traditional Hawaiian dishes. The dry, fluffy texture when cooked is quite different from typical American sweet potatoes, making it excellent for applications where you don't want excess moisture, such as tempura or french fries. In Japan, it's a premium variety commanding high prices.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Murasaki slips in loose, well-drained soil with full sun. This variety needs a longer growing season than most, so plant early when soil reaches 65°F. Space slips 12-15 inches apart in rows 36-42 inches apart. Murasaki produces vigorous vines that spread widely - ensure adequate space. The tubers develop deep in the soil, so avoid compacted areas. This variety stores exceptionally well - the dry texture improves with curing and storage. Cure at 85°F for 10-14 days for best flavor and texture development.

varieties.name: Hernandez
varieties.description: Hernandez Sweet Potato is a high-yielding variety developed by Louisiana State University, known for its uniform shape, deep orange flesh, and excellent flavor. It has copper-colored skin and produces consistently shaped tubers that are ideal for commercial production and home gardens. Hernandez offers superior disease resistance, particularly to soil-borne diseases, and has a moist, sweet flavor perfect for baking, roasting, and mashing. This variety is valued for reliability and consistent performance.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, especially during tuber formation
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Balanced fertilizer, low nitrogen, moderate feeding

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, moist, rich flavor with excellent texture

varieties.fun_fact: Hernandez was released by LSU in 1995 and was named after Dr. Tara P. Hernandez, a renowned sweet potato researcher. It quickly gained popularity with commercial growers due to its exceptional uniformity, high yields, and disease resistance. Hernandez can produce over 300 bushels per acre under optimal conditions. The variety's consistency makes it popular for processing into sweet potato products like fries and chips.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Hernandez slips in well-prepared, loose soil with good drainage. This variety performs best in sandy loam soils. Plant slips 3-4 inches deep and 12 inches apart when soil temperature reaches 65°F. Hernandez has vigorous vine growth - ensure adequate spacing between rows (36-48 inches). The excellent disease resistance makes it suitable for fields with soil-borne disease pressure. Water consistently during tuber development. Harvest when vines begin to yellow. Cure at 80-85°F with 85-90% humidity for 7-10 days for exceptional storage life.

varieties.name: White Yam
varieties.description: White Yam Sweet Potato, also called Boniato or Cuban Sweet Potato, is a unique variety with white to pale yellow flesh and burgundy to purple skin. Despite being called a 'yam,' it's a true sweet potato with a dry, fluffy texture similar to a russet potato. White Yam has a mild, slightly sweet flavor with chestnut undertones, making it perfect for savory dishes. It's popular in Latin American and Caribbean cuisines and provides an alternative to traditional orange sweet potatoes.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, prefers slightly drier conditions than orange varieties

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, slightly sweet, nutty, chestnut-like with dry, fluffy texture

root_characteristics.root_color: White to pale yellow flesh, burgundy to purple skin

varieties.fun_fact: White Yam sweet potatoes are called 'boniato' in Spanish-speaking countries and are a staple in Cuban cuisine. The name 'yam' is a misnomer - true yams are an entirely different species. Boniato's dry texture makes it perfect for dishes where you don't want the sweetness or moisture of orange sweet potatoes. In Latin American markets, boniato often commands premium prices due to high demand from Caribbean and Central American communities.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant White Yam slips in loose, sandy, well-drained soil. This variety is more drought-tolerant than orange sweet potatoes and actually prefers slightly drier conditions. Plant slips 3-4 inches deep and 12-15 inches apart when soil reaches 65-70°F. The irregular shape means tubers can grow quite large and deep - ensure soil is loose to at least 12 inches. This variety needs a full growing season to develop best flavor. Harvest carefully as the irregular shape makes tubers more prone to damage. Cure at 85°F for 10-14 days - the dry texture improves significantly with proper curing.
